newsitem.title: UK: S&P rates Scottish Life Finance sub bonds A minus.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates Scottish Life Finance sub bonds A minus.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Friday it assigned its A minus long-term rating to Scottish Life Finance Plc's nine percent 125 million sterling undated subordinated guaranteed bonds.
S&P issued the following statement.
Standard & Poor's today has assigned its A minus long-term rating to Scottish Life Finance PLC's (SLF) 9 percent 125 million sterling undated subordinated guaranteed bonds.
SLF is a new special purpose subsidiary of The Scottish Life Assurance Company (Scottish Life - financial strength rating A plus), the guarantor of the bonds.

The notes will be subordinated such that they are admissible towards the statutory capital base of Scottish Life under Department of Trade and Industry regulations. Scottish Life is positioned in the second tier of U.K. life offices and specializes in pensions business.
The financial strength and long-term ratings are based on Scottish Life's:
-- good market position;
-- good operating performance;
-- good and conservatively managed capitalization; and
-- superior service standards.
MAJOR RATING FACTORS:

-- Capitalization is good and stable. The non-linked free asset ratio was 7.2% for 1995 and has fluctuated in a narrow band between 6.2% and 7.5% since 1991. Although the 1995 ratio is relatively low compared to similarly rated companies, over time the ratios are among the most stable of all companies. The with-profits free asset ratio is similarly stable (range 11.4%-12.1%) as is the coverage of minimum margin (2.4 times (x) - 2.7x).

This stability reflects the company's Appointed Actuary's policy in closely reflecting bond yields in valuing liabilities. Reversionary bonuses were cut again in 1995 as a continuation towards a level that Scottish Life believe to be sustainable for the long term. Policy proceeds continue to mirror asset shares closely. On a pro-forma basis the bond increases the 1995 non-linked free asset ratio from 7.2% to 9.2% and coverage of minimum margin from 2.7x to 3.2x. Scottish Life remains committed to mutuality and its financial flexibility is limited as a result. The higher level of capitalization is offset by the utilization of some of this flexibility.

-- Good U.K. market position, with approximately 4% of the IFA life and pensions market. Scottish Life performed relatively well in 1995 in adverse market conditions. Sales (in terms of regular premium plus 10% of single premiums) were down by only 4%, whereas sales in the U.K. market overall were down some 17%. The life and pensions market is looking healthier today than a year ago. Scottish Life's sales, year to Nov. 30, 1996, were up by 9.3% compared to 1995 at the same stage.

-- Good expense levels. Although lower sales in 1994 and 1995 adversely affected the company's expense competitiveness, Standard & Poor's believes that 1997 will mark a return to full coverage of actual expenses by margins. This can be attributed both to higher prospective sales in 1997 and expense reductions during 1996. Expense ratios are consistent with the rating level (total expense ratio 17.1%, acquisition expense ratio 81.2% and maintenance expense ratio 8.7%).

-- Scottish Life's superior service standards are evidenced by the "Financial Adviser" 5 star award which was retained for the third consecutive year. Standard & Poor's believes that this is due to Scottish Life's strong focus on the IFA sector and, in part, to the company's administration systems which have been completely rewritten, a process which many of its peers have only partly completed.
OUTLOOK: Stable.
-- Moderate sales growth in medium term, potential for much stronger growth in the longer term.
-- Capitalization remaining stable with coverage of the minimum margin likely to exceed three times over the long term.
-- Expense base managed to continue to reflect available loadings.
-- Continued excellent service standards, Standard & Poor's said. -- CreditWire Contact: Rob Jones, London (44) 171-826-3650 Reply to tlx 7608140 via CCI.
